result.title: Can an LLM Fix a Language Model Without Training It?
result.summary: Although an external language model can select and test repairs to another model's weights, behavior can also be recovered through fixed numerical edits. We assessed the value of interactive selection in a controlled study of Transformer repair. After inspecting predictions, activation summaries, and weight statistics, the editor selects projection recipes to apply to the target without gradient updates. We analyzed 20 recorded sessions involving five masked and causal language models, comparing the selected edits with fixed projections, scripted and matched-budget black-box search, and low-rank adaptation. Under the core two-layer fault, live selection matches black-box search on SmolLM2 and Qwen2.5. For Pythia, live selection achieves 65.62% completion accuracy, compared with 0% for black-box search and 66.15% for a fixed projection. Under a separate compound fault affecting attention and feed-forward weights, both scripted and LLM-guided selection increase the descriptive five-checkpoint mean from 24.89% to 71.25% using the same operator family. On unmodified checkpoints, scripted projection yields small gains or losses on a separate set of framed questions. The experiments identify cases in which feedback changes an edit decision, operator coverage accounts for recovery, or supervised adaptation performs better. Combined with measurements of parameter restoration and preservation, these comparisons establish the scope of controller-guided repair for the tested faults and completion tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在受控的 Transformer 修复任务中，让外部 LLM 依据预测、激活摘要和权重统计选择无梯度的投影编辑，并与固定投影、脚本化及等预算黑盒搜索、LoRA 对比，评估交互选择是否带来增益。
AI.relevance_reason: 「外部控制器读取激活摘要后决定干预」这一范式可能为 LVR 中由控制器检查并修改 latent 推理状态提供可核查线索；但该作无视觉输入、目标是权重修复而非推理状态生成，迁移性需自行判断。
